claims.evidence: StatPearls: acts on the parietal cell's final step of acid production.
Pharmacology abstracts: active form binds the H+/K+ ATPase (gastric proton pump) in parietal cells.
Attributed to StatPearls but StatPearls snippet did not say this; 'builds up inside cells' not in any retrieved text. PubMed abstract supports prodrug/activated in parietal cell/irreversible binding.
claims.newSentence: A review of its pharmacology says omeprazole is a prodrug, changed to its active form only in the acid-making cells, where it binds irreversibly to the proton pump.

claims.evidence: 'Lasts longer than the drug stays in blood' is inference; abstract says long-lasting inhibition of acid secretion.
claims.newSentence: This gives an effective and long-lasting reduction in stomach acid.

'Study in healthy volunteers' per product information was not retrieved. SPS text: CYP2C19 activates clopidogrel; omeprazole/esomeprazole inhibit it, reducing activated clopidogrel.
claims.newSentence: The Specialist Pharmacy Service, part of the NHS, explains that clopidogrel is activated by an enzyme called CYP2C19, and that omeprazole and esomeprazole inhibit this enzyme, which can lower the level of activated clopidogrel.

claims.evidence: Source is SPS (NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service), not an NHS patient page: 'use lansoprazole, pantoprazole or rabeprazole in preference'. Attribution fixed. Note gov.uk says evidence does not support extending the advice beyond omeprazole/esomeprazole.
claims.newSentence: The Specialist Pharmacy Service says lansoprazole, pantoprazole or rabeprazole are preferred to omeprazole for people taking clopidogrel.

notes: Search summaries blend pages, so URL attribution within nhs.uk/medicines/omeprazole/ is by page topic, not verified per sentence. Kidney/liver/osteoporosis list cited to how-and-when page (who-can-and-cannot page was not returned; list incomplete in retrieved text). Alcohol, long-term, cancer-symptom sentences cited to common-questions page (it was returned for those queries). Clopidogrel alternatives are SPS (NHS Specialist Pharmacy Service) guidance, not an NHS patient page; gov.uk DSU says evidence does not support extending the avoid advice beyond omeprazole/esomeprazole. Pregnancy wording: one search summary said 'safe' but that was the summariser; final text uses only 'usually can be taken; check first'. Capsules prescription-only came from one NHS-page summary; another summary said all types available on prescription (compatible). Textbook: one (999 for anaphylaxis). Removed: schedule wording, steady claims about masking cancer symptoms, SmPC monitoring, StatPearls interaction list, citalopram. Search cap of 8 reached.
